Robust combination on a metric-ranked subset: tests whether selecting top-7 by SMAPE and trimming worst tail beats full-pool robust combos, motivated by unstable ranking and one large correlated error group.
Per-horizon top-k weighting on the 7-model pool to exploit unstable cross-window rankings (tau=0.228) and seasonal regime where different models win at different horizons
DBA optimizes convex weights on pool4, a different combination kind than the trimmed_mean leader; may better capture per-horizon model dominance in this seasonal series
Median on the best pool (pool4) as a different robust aggregator than trimmed_mean; with 7 models it takes the 4th value, robust to one outlier model but different from trimming 20% (1.4 models).

Median on pool4+NaiveMovingAverage: adds the only always-top3 model (best last-window SMAPE 0.0583) to the robust pool, testing whether a consistently strong model improves the median in an unstable-ranking regime
Per-horizon top-5 weighting on the 7-model pool4; captures horizon-specific model strengths in a strongly seasonal series with unstable rankings
Zero outliers and stable seasonal signal suggest mean may match median without the robustness overhead; tests whether the leader's median advantage is meaningful or just noise.

Soft exponential weighting on the 7-model pool: gives more weight to lower-error models while remaining robust to the highly correlated pool (mean_corr=0.941) and unstable ranking (tau=0.228). Different mechanism from median leader.

decision.justification: Selected 'median on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8275. Series context: trend strength 0.2747 and seasonal strength 0.9902; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.228); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.408.
